body.answer: Controloc contains Pantoprazole. This drug is used for reducing stomach acid secretion, and treating GERD and Peptic Ulcers, and is part of H. pylori treatment regimens. Common side effects include Headache, Nausea, Abdominal pain, Diarrhea or constipation, and Flatulence. Long-term use may carry a risk of Vitamin B12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia, and increased susceptibility to certain intestinal infections. Contraindications and precautions include hypersensitivity to PPIs and reviewing drug interactions, especially with Clopidogrel in the case of Omeprazole and Esomeprazole. Alarm symptoms like unexplained weight loss, dysphagia, or GI bleeding require medical evaluation rather than just continuing PPI use.

body.answer: Local anesthetic sprays or lozenges used for a sore throat include B.B.C Spray, Strepsils Plus, and Orofar. These are used to temporarily relieve throat pain by causing local numbness, often in the form of sprays or lozenges. Common side effects can include temporary numbness of the mouth and throat, burning or irritation, altered taste, and allergic reactions. Toxicity from Lidocaine can occur with overuse or large amounts ingested. Benzocaine may rarely cause Methemoglobinemia. Contraindications include hypersensitivity to local anesthetics or any formulation component. Benzocaine use requires extreme caution, and lozenges are indicated for ages 12 and older.

body.answer: Brufen, which contains Ibuprofen, requires medical evaluation during pregnancy starting from week 20. NSAIDs are generally avoided from week 30 of pregnancy.
